title: Logarithmic improvement conjecture for defective colouring of linear hypergraphs
statement:
Let $r\geqslant 1$, let $\Delta$ be the maximum degree, and let $d\geqslant 2$. A hypergraph is **linear** if every two distinct edges intersect in at most one vertex. A $d$-defective $k$-colouring is a colouring of the vertices with $k$ colours such that every colour class induces maximum degree at most $d$.

**Defective-colouring conjecture.** Every $(r+1)$-uniform linear hypergraph with maximum degree at most $\Delta$ has a $d$-defective colouring with

$$
\nk=\mathcal{O}\left(\left(\frac{\Delta}{\log\Delta}\cdot\frac{\log d}{d}\right)^{1/r}\right).
$$

This would match the lower bound obtained from known examples of linear hypergraphs, up to the implicit constant, and would establish a logarithmic improvement over the general defective-colouring bound for sparse hypergraphs. The conjecture is presented as open in the source.
source_name: António Girão, Freddie Illingworth, Alex Scott and David R. Wood, “Defective Colouring of Hypergraphs”, arXiv:2207.10514 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.10514

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2022).
